title: Meta pauses Muse sharing after researchers find AI chats on the web
slides: Meta's AI chats surfaced on the open web. What leaked?
Muse conversations were meant to stay private
But public URLs exposed chats to anyone searching
Check your AI chat links before you share them
Ask: who can find your prompts tomorrow?
thread_text:
1. Your AI chats went public

Meta's AI conversations, including Muse, were indexed by search engines. Private chats became search results for anyone.

2. Muse was supposed to be private

The whole point of a private conversation is that it stays private. These weren't meant to leave the chat window.

3. Public links, no lock

Each chat had a shareable URL. No password, no login wall. Anyone with the link could read the whole thing.

4. Search engines don't forget

Once indexed, the chat could show up in results for anyone searching relevant keywords. Deleting the link may not be enough.

5. Who can find your prompts?

Check every AI chat link you have shared. Ask yourself: if this showed up in a search tomorrow, would you be okay with that?

instagram.caption:
Your private conversation with Meta's AI may have been readable by anyone with the link.

Muse chats were meant to stay between you and the bot, but each one had a shareable URL with no password or login wall. Search engines indexed them.

That means a prompt you thought was private could surface in results for anyone searching the right words—and deleting the link may not be enough once it's cached.

If you write or publish anything, assume your past AI chats could be found tomorrow. 🔍

Go through every AI chat link you've shared and ask yourself: would you be okay if this showed up in a search? 💬
